Pick, per feature, the capture nearest a date

Source: R/dft_wayback_pick.R
dft_wayback_pick.Rd

From the captures table of dft_wayback_captures(), keeps for each feature and each target date the one capture whose acquisition date is nearest to it. The result names the release and zoom to pass to dft_wayback_fetch().

Usage

dft_wayback_pick(captures, date)

Arguments

captures

A captures table from dft_wayback_captures(). Any table with feature, capture_date and res_m works; release_date, release_id and cover are used as tiebreaks when present.

date

A Date vector (or character coercible by as.Date()) of target dates. Duplicates are dropped.

Value

A tibble with one row per feature and target date, for every feature that has a dated capture: feature, date, the chosen capture's other columns, and days_from_date (signed: negative is a capture before the date). A feature with no capture has no row; merge with your feature ids to list it. Sorted by feature, then date.

Details

Captures are ranked by, in order:

  1. days between capture_date and date, either side;

  2. finer res_m;

  3. the later release_date, then the larger release_id (compared as a number). The same capture is usually served by many releases, and any of them fetches it: a release that has not changed a tile redirects to the release that last did;

  4. the larger cover, then the earlier capture_date, then source, so the order is total even for a polygon that shows two captures equally near the date in one release.

Cover enters only as a tiebreak. For polygons, filter on cover before the pick when the capture must image most of each feature.

A study design that bands by whole years (a capture in the endpoint year before any capture a year off) expresses the band through the date: pass mid-season, e.g. as.Date("2017-07-01"), and check days_from_date in the result. The ranking itself does not band.

See also

dft_wayback_captures(), dft_wayback_fetch().

Examples

cap <- tibble::tibble(
  feature = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L),
  release_id = c("100", "200", "300", "300"),
  release_date = as.Date(c("2017-11-16", "2020-04-29", "2024-03-07", "2024-03-07")),
  capture_date = as.Date(c("2013-08-01", "2017-06-11", "2023-08-25", "2016-09-30")),
  res_m = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 0.5),
  source = "Maxar WV02", zoom = 18L, cover = 1
)
# the capture nearest mid-season in each endpoint year
dft_wayback_pick(cap, as.Date(c("2017-07-01", "2023-07-01")))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 10
#>   feature date       release_id release_date capture_date res_m source      zoom
#>     <int> <date>     <chr>      <date>       <date>       <dbl> <chr>      <int>
#> 1       1 2017-07-01 200        2020-04-29   2017-06-11     0.5 Maxar WV02    18
#> 2       1 2023-07-01 300        2024-03-07   2023-08-25     0.3 Maxar WV02    18
#> 3       2 2017-07-01 300        2024-03-07   2016-09-30     0.5 Maxar WV02    18
#> 4       2 2023-07-01 300        2024-03-07   2016-09-30     0.5 Maxar WV02    18
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: cover <dbl>, days_from_date <int>
